intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square at Dusk
experiences.description: Experience the legendary main square of Marrakech as it transforms at sunset into a spectacular open-air theatre. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform while sampling freshly squeezed orange juice and traditional Moroccan street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and grilled merguez sausages from the famous food stalls.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset, arriving at a traditional Berber nomad camp for an unforgettable night under a sky blazing with stars. Enjoy a tagine dinner cooked over an open fire, listen to Gnawa drumming and music around the campfire, and wake at dawn to witness the sunrise paint the dunes in shades of amber and rose.

experiences.name: Medina Souks & Tanneries Walking Tour
experiences.description: Hire a local guide to navigate the labyrinthine medieval souks of Marrakech, exploring the ancient leather tanneries of the Chouara district where hides are still dyed using centuries-old methods. Visit the spice souk, the lantern makers, and the carpet weavers while learning about the history of trade along the trans-Saharan caravan routes that made Marrakech a legendary imperial city.
experiences.location: Northern Medina Souks & Chouara Tannery, Marrakech

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local Marrakchi family or a riad-based chef for a hands-on cooking class beginning with a guided tour of the Mellah spice market to select fresh ingredients. Learn to prepare authentic dishes including chicken bastilla, lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives, and honey-drenched chebakia pastries, gaining deep insight into the Berber, Arab, and Andalusian culinary heritage that defines Moroccan cuisine.

experiences.name: Aït Benhaddou Kasbah & Draa Valley Exploration
experiences.description: Take a day trip to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Aït Benhaddou, a breathtaking fortified mud-brick village that has served as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue through the lush Draa Valley, Morocco's longest river valley, stopping at ancient kasbahs, Berber villages, and date palm oases while a local guide shares the rich history of the Glaoui dynasty and trans-Saharan trade.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take the 19 bus or a shared petit taxi (negotiate to ~50–70 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the quiet night streets of Derb Sidi Bouloukat to get your bearings. Rest early to prepare for a full Day 2.

meals.breakfast: N/A – on the plane
meals.lunch: N/A – on the plane
meals.dinner: If hungry on arrival, grab a quick snack from a late-night street cart near Jemaa el-Fna (open until midnight) – msemen flatbread or a harira soup for ~10–15 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Keep small change (MAD) ready for the taxi. Hotel Aday is a budget riad in the heart of the Medina – confirm your late check-in with them in advance. Exchange some currency at the airport (small amount) or use an ATM inside arrivals for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, walk 10 minutes to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere – orange juice vendors, snake charmers setting up, and locals heading to work. Then explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only, non-Muslims cannot enter) and the surrounding souks. Head into the Souk Semmarine for a sensory overload of spices, leather, and textiles. Bargaining is expected – enjoy the experience without pressure to buy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD / ~$7 USD) – a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan architecture, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the old Mellah market for a glimpse into Marrakech's multicultural history. Stop at the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) – a beautifully preserved royal necropolis from the 16th century.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as the square transforms into a massive open-air food market. Watch the storytellers, musicians, and acrobats. Dine at one of the numbered food stalls (stalls 1–100) – try grilled merguez sausages, kefta brochettes, and Moroccan salads for ~50–80 MAD total. Walk back through the lit-up souks before heading to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Café de France or a local café near the hotel – café au lait + msemen or beghrir (Moroccan pancakes) with honey and butter for ~20–30 MAD
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant in the souks – try a set menu (menu du jour) with harira soup, tagine, and mint tea for ~50–70 MAD at places like Restaurant Chez Bahia
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled meats, Moroccan salads, and fresh-squeezed orange juice for ~60–90 MAD total

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Keep your bag close in crowded areas. The Saadian Tombs and Bahia Palace are within 15 minutes' walk of the hotel. Avoid accepting unsolicited 'guides' in the souks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entrance ~70 MAD) – one of the most beautiful Islamic schools in North Africa, featuring intricate zellige tilework, carved stucco, and a serene central courtyard. It's a 10-minute walk from the hotel. Afterward, explore the nearby Musée de Marrakech (entrance ~50 MAD) housed in a 19th-century palace. Then wander through the Dyers' Quarter (Souk des Teinturiers) to see wool being dyed in vivid colors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Majorelle Garden (entrance ~150 MAD for garden + Berber Museum) – a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. It's about 3 km from the hotel; take a petit taxi (~20–30 MAD). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the exotic plants and the small Berber Museum inside. Walk back through the Gueliz (Ville Nouvelle) neighborhood to see the contrast between the modern French-built city and the ancient Medina.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Mouassine neighborhood – one of Marrakech's most atmospheric quarters with beautiful fountains, artisan workshops, and hidden riads. Have dinner at a local neighborhood restaurant away from the tourist center for better prices. End the evening with a traditional hammam experience at a local hammam (not a tourist spa) – try Hammam Dar el-Bacha for ~50–80 MAD for a basic scrub session.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or a nearby café – Moroccan mint tea, khobz bread with olive oil and amlou (argan oil almond paste) for ~25 MAD
meals.lunch: Street food near Ben Youssef Madrasa – a bowl of bissara (fava bean soup with olive oil and cumin) and fresh bread for ~15–20 MAD, or a sandwich from a local snack shop for ~20–30 MAD
meals.dinner: Restaurant in Mouassine quarter – chicken or lamb tagine with couscous and Moroccan salad for ~60–80 MAD at a non-tourist local spot

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden online in advance if possible – it can sell out, especially on weekends. The hammam is a must-do cultural experience; bring flip-flops and a change of clothes. Negotiate taxi fares before getting in.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a shared/group day-tour or budget overnight tour. Book through your hotel or a local agency the night before – a 2-day/1-night shared group tour to Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes) costs approximately 600–900 MAD per person from Marrakech, including transport, accommodation in a desert camp, and camel ride. The route passes through the stunning Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains – enjoy dramatic views of snow-capped peaks and Berber villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar (ancient fortified village) – one of Morocco's most iconic sights, used as a filming location for Game of Thrones and Gladiator. Explore the mud-brick kasbah for 1–2 hours (entrance ~10 MAD). Continue driving through the Draa Valley, passing date palm oases, rose fields (if in season), and dramatic desert landscapes toward Ouarzazate and beyond.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga around sunset. Mount camels for a 45-minute ride into the dunes to your desert camp. Watch the sunset over the Sahara – one of the most breathtaking experiences in Morocco. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner at the camp under a sky full of stars, with live Gnawa music around a campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure – bread, jam, and mint tea (~20–30 MAD or included in hotel)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate – tagine or sandwich for ~40–60 MAD (often included in tour packages)
meals.dinner: Included in the desert camp package – traditional Berber tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara tour 1–2 days in advance through Hotel Aday or a reputable local agency. Compare prices from at least 3 agencies. Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Pack sunscreen, sunglasses, a headscarf for the dunes, and a power bank. The drive is approximately 8–9 hours each way.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the dunes and watch the sunrise over the Sahara – an unforgettable golden spectacle. Take photos, explore the dunes on foot, and enjoy the silence of the desert. Return to camp for a traditional Moroccan breakfast. If time allows, visit the nearby village of Merzouga to see local Berber life and the small lake (Dayet Srji) that attracts flamingos in spring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey to Marrakech. The route back may take a different road through the Todra Gorge or Dades Valley (depending on your tour). Stop at a local argan oil cooperative (free entry, no obligation to buy) to learn how Berber women produce argan oil – a fascinating cultural stop. Continue driving through the Atlas Mountains with scenic stops.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech around 20:00–21:00. Drop bags at Hotel Aday, freshen up, and head to Jemaa el-Fna for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner and reflect on the desert experience. Early night to recover from the long journey.

meals.breakfast: Included at the desert camp – Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, argan oil, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside stop en route – tagine or sandwich at a local restaurant for ~40–60 MAD (sometimes included in tour)
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech – a simple, hearty meal at a local restaurant near the hotel, such as a bowl of harira + kefta tagine for ~50–70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Tip your camel guide and camp staff if satisfied – 20–50 MAD per person is appreciated. Stay hydrated during the drive back. If you feel adventurous, ask your tour guide about sandboarding on the dunes in the morning before departure.

day_by_day.morning: A slower, recovery morning. After breakfast, visit the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) – a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now in atmospheric ruins, with storks nesting on the walls and great views from the ramparts. Spend 1–1.5 hours exploring. Then walk along the ancient Medina walls toward the Bab Agnaou gate – one of the most beautiful original city gates of Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) in depth – visit the Lazama Synagogue (free or small donation), the old Jewish cemetery, and the covered Mellah market. This is a quieter, less-touristy part of the Medina with fascinating history. Afterward, take a cooking class or visit a spice shop in the souks to learn about Moroccan spices – ras el hanout, cumin, saffron, and preserved lemons. Many spice vendors offer free demonstrations.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a rooftop dinner with views of the Medina and Koutoubia Mosque – Café Clock or a similar rooftop restaurant offers good value at ~80–120 MAD for a full meal. Alternatively, do a final Jemaa el-Fna evening walk, buy souvenirs (bargain hard – start at 30–40% of the asking price), and enjoy fresh-squeezed orange juice (5 MAD per glass) from the square's vendors.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café – Moroccan mint tea, msemen, and amlou for ~25–35 MAD
meals.lunch: Try a traditional Moroccan pastilla (pigeon or chicken pie with almonds and powdered sugar) at a local restaurant – ~50–70 MAD, or a cheap sandwich from a Medina snack shop for ~20–30 MAD
meals.dinner: Rooftop café or a sit-down restaurant – chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives + Moroccan salad + mint tea for ~80–120 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is market day in many Moroccan cities – the souks will be busier and more vibrant. This is a great day to buy last-minute souvenirs: leather goods, argan oil, spices, and handmade ceramics. Always bargain respectfully. The Lazama Synagogue may have limited hours – check locally.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Wake up early for one last walk through the Medina before the crowds arrive – the souks are magical and quiet in the early morning light. Visit the Mouassine Fountain and the Chrob ou Chouf Fountain (beautiful carved cedar canopy). Stop at a local bakery (farran) to buy fresh-baked khobz bread and msemen for a picnic breakfast – ~5–10 MAD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, visit any missed sights or revisit favorites. Consider a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina. Pack your bags, check out of Hotel Aday, and arrange transport to the airport. The 19 bus runs to the airport for ~4 MAD, or a petit taxi costs ~50–70 MAD (negotiate in advance). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech Menara Airport. Carry some leftover MAD for airport snacks or convert back to your home currency (note: MAD is a closed currency – convert before leaving Morocco or at the airport).

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread from a local bakery + café au lait at a neighborhood café – ~15–25 MAD for a very local, authentic final breakfast
meals.lunch: Light meal near the hotel before checkout – a bowl of harira soup + bread for ~15–20 MAD, or a final street food snack from the souks
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight – grab a snack at the airport if needed

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: The total trip cost for 7 days in Morocco on a budget (excluding flights) can be kept to approximately 2,500–3,500 MAD (~$250–$350 USD) per person, covering accommodation at Hotel Aday (~150–200 MAD/night), meals (~100–150 MAD/day), transport, entrance fees, and the Sahara tour. Always carry cash in MAD as many local vendors and small restaurants do not accept cards.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or ask the hotel for a late-night recommendation close to Derb Sidi Bouloukat

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and a late arrival mean rest is the priority. Confirm your hotel has 24-hour reception or arrange a late check-in in advance. Exchange some currency to Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) at the airport for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Then walk 10 minutes to Jemaa el-Fna Square to soak in the morning atmosphere – orange juice vendors, bread sellers, and locals heading to work. From there, explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior view) and stroll into the historic souks of the Medina – spice souk, leather souk, and the dyers' quarter (Chouara-style small tanneries in Marrakech).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century riad-style palace with ornate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, head to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD) for a taste of Marrakech's layered history. Take a slow walk back through the southern Medina streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a vibrant open-air spectacle – snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and dozens of food stalls. Enjoy dinner at one of the square's food stalls or a rooftop restaurant overlooking the action.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Café des Épices nearby – mint tea, msemen (Moroccan flatbread), honey, and amlou (almond-argan dip) – ~30–50 MAD
meals.lunch: Snack in the souks – fresh-squeezed orange juice (4 MAD), a kefta sandwich, or a bowl of harira soup from a local stall – ~40–70 MAD
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls (stall #1–32 area) – try merguez sausages, grilled lamb chops, and Moroccan salads – ~80–120 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina streets are cobblestoned and uneven. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep a small bag close to you in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Then explore the Maison de la Photographie de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) for a fascinating visual history of Morocco through vintage photographs. Walk through the northern Medina toward the Ben Youssef Medersa (entry ~70 MAD), one of the most exquisite examples of Islamic architecture in North Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum complex (garden entry ~150 MAD, Berber Museum included; YSL Museum ~100 MAD extra). The cobalt-blue garden designed by Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent is a peaceful oasis. Afterward, explore the Gueliz neighborhood (New City) for a change of pace – browse art galleries and modern Moroccan boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Medina for a relaxed evening. Explore the area around Mouassine Fountain and the upscale boutique-lined streets nearby. Enjoy a sit-down dinner at a traditional Moroccan restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or Café Clock Marrakech near the Medina – Moroccan pancakes (baghrir), coffee, and fresh juice – ~40–60 MAD
meals.lunch: Nomad Restaurant near the Saadian Tombs – modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views – ~100–150 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Le Foundouk or a similar mid-range riad restaurant in the Medina – lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, couscous, and pastilla – ~150–200 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance – it sells out quickly, especially on weekends. March weather in Marrakech is mild (15–22°C), so a light jacket for evenings is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a shared or private day-tour to the Draa Valley and Zagora region, OR begin the longer journey toward Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes) if you've pre-booked a 2-day desert excursion. The route passes through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas Mountains – stop for photos and a Berber tea break at a roadside café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Ouarzazate – the 'Hollywood of Africa.' Stop at Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage ksar/fortified village, entry ~10 MAD), used as a filming location for Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia. Explore the ancient earthen towers and walk across the river to the village. Have lunch here before continuing toward the desert.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp near Zagora or continue to Merzouga depending on your tour. If at Zagora: enjoy a sunset camel ride into the dunes (~100–150 MAD for 1 hour). Settle into a mid-range desert camp with Berber tents, enjoy a traditional dinner under the stars, and experience live Gnawa music around a campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure – pack snacks for the road
meals.lunch: Restaurant at Aït Benhaddou village – Berber tagine and fresh bread – ~80–120 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Included at the desert camp – traditional Moroccan feast: harira, tagine, couscous, and Moroccan pastries – typically included in camp package (~400–600 MAD per person for camp + dinner + breakfast)

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable desert tour operator in advance from Marrakech – look for tours that include Aït Benhaddou, transport, camel ride, and overnight camp. Shared tours cost ~600–900 MAD per person; private tours ~1,500–2,500 MAD. Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–8°C. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, and a scarf for sand.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) for a magical desert sunrise over the dunes – one of the most memorable experiences in Morocco. Take a short morning walk or camel ride to a high dune for panoramic views. Enjoy a traditional Berber breakfast at camp (mint tea, bread, olive oil, honey, and eggs). Begin the return journey toward Marrakech, stopping at scenic viewpoints along the Draa Valley's palm groves and kasbahs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Ouarzazate for a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios (entry ~80 MAD) – the world's largest film studio, where you can see massive sets from famous productions. Continue the drive back through the Atlas Mountains, arriving in Marrakech by late afternoon (around 17:00–18:00). Check back into Hotel Aday and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle evening in the Medina to recover from the long journey. Visit the hammam for a traditional Moroccan bath and scrub (mid-range hammam ~150–250 MAD for full treatment). Afterward, enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp – traditional Berber breakfast
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant en route – tagine and Moroccan salad – ~70–100 MAD
meals.dinner: Riad Yima or a local Medina restaurant near Derb Sidi Bouloukat – chicken bastilla (sweet-savory pigeon pie) and mint tea – ~120–160 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Zagora is approximately 6–7 hours; from Merzouga it's 9–10 hours. Factor in rest stops. If you feel the drive is too long, consider an overnight in Ouarzazate to break the journey. Confirm your hotel reservation for the return night.

day_by_day.morning: A slower, culturally rich morning in Marrakech. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century palace – excellent collection of Moroccan art, ceramics, and manuscripts. Then take a guided walking tour of the Medina's hidden derbs (alleyways) and artisan workshops – many hotels can arrange a local guide (~200–300 MAD for 2 hours) for an authentic behind-the-scenes experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi ride (~20 MAD) to the Palmeraie (palm grove) on the outskirts of Marrakech for a relaxed afternoon. You can rent a bicycle or take a calèche (horse-drawn carriage) ride through the palm trees (~150–200 MAD for 1 hour). Alternatively, visit the Agdal Gardens (free entry) – vast royal orchards and gardens south of the Medina, perfect for a peaceful afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a special farewell-to-Marrakech dinner at a rooftop restaurant or a traditional riad with live music. Afterward, do final souvenir shopping in the souks – argan oil, leather goods, Moroccan lanterns, and spices make great gifts.

meals.breakfast: Café des Épices on Place Rahba Kedima – fresh-squeezed juice, Moroccan pancakes, and coffee with a view of the spice market – ~40–60 MAD
meals.lunch: Mechoui Alley (Rue Bab Marrakech, near Jemaa el-Fna) – slow-roasted whole lamb sold by weight, eaten with bread and cumin – ~60–80 MAD per person (a true local institution)
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout or a similar atmospheric riad restaurant – full Moroccan feast with live Andalusian music – ~250–350 MAD per person (book in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Mechoui Alley is best visited at lunch when the lamb is freshly roasted – arrive by 12:30 PM before it sells out. For souvenir shopping, the fixed-price cooperatives (argan oil cooperatives, carpet cooperatives) offer fair prices without the pressure of bargaining.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Take one last stroll through Jemaa el-Fna and the surrounding souks to pick up any last-minute souvenirs or gifts. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens one more time for a peaceful farewell moment – the 12th-century minaret is most beautiful in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Hotel Aday (standard checkout is 12:00 PM – ask about late checkout if your flight is in the evening). Store luggage at the hotel if needed. Spend remaining time at a rooftop café with views over the Medina, journaling or simply absorbing the atmosphere of Marrakech one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange airport transfer (petit taxi ~80–100 MAD or pre-booked transfer ~150–200 MAD). Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at least 2.5–3 hours before your departure flight. Enjoy a final mint tea at the airport.

meals.breakfast: Grand Café de la Poste in Gueliz (if checking out early) or hotel breakfast – croissants, Moroccan pastries, coffee – ~50–80 MAD
meals.lunch: Café Arabe near the Mouassine Fountain – light mezze, Moroccan salads, and fresh lemonade – ~100–130 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or pack Moroccan pastries (chebakia, ghriba cookies) from the souks as a travel snack

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech Menara Airport is only 6 km from the Medina – about 15–20 minutes by taxi. Confirm your flight time and allow extra time for airport security. Declare any argan oil over 100ml in checked luggage. Keep a small amount of MAD for tips and last-minute expenses, but note that leftover dirhams can be difficult to exchange outside Morocco.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport to Hotel Aday in the Medina. A dedicated concierge will greet you at arrivals with a name board. Check-in, unwind with a welcome mint tea and traditional pastries prepared by the riad.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in-flight.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival and hotel check-in only. Light room service or a curated welcome amenity tray awaits in your suite. Rest and acclimatize.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: In-flight
meals.dinner: Light room service at Hotel Aday upon arrival — request a traditional harira soup, msemen flatbread, and fresh Moroccan orange juice with orange blossom water

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport pickup in advance with Hotel Aday. Confirm your private transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar luxury vehicle) before departure. Keep Day 1 completely relaxed — the Medina can be overwhelming at night for first-timers.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the riad rooftop terrace. Then embark on a private guided walking tour of the Marrakech Medina — begin with the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square in the calm morning hours before the crowds arrive. Explore the labyrinthine souks: spice market (Rahba Kedima), the dyers' souk, and the leather goods quarter. Visit the 14th-century Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most stunning examples of Moroccan Islamic architecture, with its intricate zellige tilework and carved cedar wood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Saadian Tombs — a hidden royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring exquisite Italian Carrara marble and gold-leaf decoration. Continue to the El Badi Palace ruins, a 16th-century palace once described as one of the wonders of the world. Stroll through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and visit the Lazama Synagogue. Return to the riad for a traditional hammam and spa treatment — book the hotel's premium hammam package (black soap scrub, ghassoul clay mask, argan oil massage).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop of a luxury bar overlooking the Koutoubia Mosque minaret. Dinner at Le Jardin Secret Restaurant or Dar Yacout — a legendary Marrakchi palace restaurant offering a full traditional Moroccan feast: pastilla au pigeon, slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives, couscous royale, and bastilla au lait for dessert, accompanied by live Gnawa music.

meals.breakfast: Riad rooftop breakfast — fresh-squeezed orange juice, msemen with argan oil and honey, Moroccan mint tea, soft-boiled eggs, seasonal fruit platter, and baghrir (semolina pancakes)
meals.lunch: Café des Épices on Place Rahba Kedima — rooftop terrace with Medina views; try the kefta brochettes, zaalouk (smoky eggplant salad), and fresh-squeezed pomegranate juice
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout — full traditional Moroccan banquet in a stunning 1930s palace setting; budget approximately 800–1,200 MAD per person; reservations essential

day_by_day.notes: Hire a licensed private guide for the Medina tour (avoid unofficial guides). Wear comfortable walking shoes — Medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. The Ben Youssef Madrasa opens at 09:00. Book Dar Yacout well in advance as it fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden — the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Arrive early (09:00 opening) to beat the crowds. Explore the Berber Museum within the garden, housing an extraordinary collection of Amazigh jewelry, textiles, and artifacts. Walk through the adjacent Islamic Art Museum of Marrakech (MIAM) for a curated collection of Moroccan decorative arts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Musée de Marrakech housed in the 19th-century Mnebhi Palace — admire its stunning central courtyard with a massive brass chandelier. Then explore the Mouassine neighborhood — one of the Medina's most atmospheric quarters — visiting the 16th-century Mouassine Mosque fountain and the concept boutiques along Rue Mouassine. Enjoy a private Moroccan cooking class at a traditional riad kitchen: learn to make harira soup, chicken bastilla, and a classic tagine with a master chef.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the rooftop of Café du Livre or the Sky Bar at La Mamounia Hotel (request day access or book a drink reservation). Dinner at Nomad Restaurant — a contemporary Moroccan cuisine restaurant with a stunning rooftop terrace overlooking the spice market; known for its modern reinterpretations of Moroccan classics.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Aday riad breakfast — expanded spread with amlou (almond-argan dip), fresh Medjool dates, Moroccan crepes, and a selection of local cheeses
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café Kif Kif or Terrasse des Épices — mezze-style sharing plates: hummus, briouats, grilled vegetables, and fresh-baked khobz bread
meals.dinner: Nomad Restaurant, Derb Aarjan — modern Moroccan tasting menu; try the lamb mechoui, preserved lemon risotto, and the chocolate-orange blossom fondant; approximately 600–900 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden tickets should be booked online in advance (sells out). The cooking class can be arranged through the hotel concierge — budget 800–1,200 MAD per person for a premium private session. La Mamounia rooftop access may require a reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (06:00–07:00) by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the journey to the Sahara Desert via the dramatic Draa Valley and Dades Gorge route. Drive through the High Atlas Mountains — stop at the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260m elevation) for panoramic mountain views and photos. Continue through Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa' — for a brief stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou Ksar, a stunning fortified mud-brick village used as a filming location for Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of Aït Benhaddou with a local Berber guide — climb to the top granary for sweeping views of the surrounding palmery and Draa Valley. Continue driving through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) near Kelaat M'Gouna, famous for its Damask rose cultivation. Stop at a local cooperative to learn about rose water and argan oil production. Arrive at Merzouga (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) by late afternoon — check in to your luxury desert camp or boutique desert lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Mount your private camel for a guided sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the tallest sand dunes in Morocco (up to 150m). Watch the sunset paint the dunes in shades of gold, amber, and crimson. Arrive at your exclusive luxury desert camp: private Berber tent with en-suite bathroom, plush bedding, and lantern lighting. Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner under a canopy of stars with live Gnawa and Berber music around a campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure — packed premium breakfast box for the road: dates, nuts, Moroccan pastries, thermos of mint tea
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber lunch at a family-run restaurant in Ouarzazate or near Aït Benhaddou — lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, Moroccan salads, fresh bread, and mint tea
meals.dinner: Luxury desert camp dinner — full Berber feast: harira, mechoui lamb slow-roasted in a sand pit, couscous with seven vegetables, fresh fruit, and Moroccan pastries; mint tea and coffee under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours with stops — an early start is essential. Ensure your private driver is licensed and the vehicle is a proper 4x4 for desert terrain. Recommended luxury desert camps: Scarabeo Camp, Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp, or Merzouga Luxury Desert Camp — book well in advance. Bring warm layers — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn (05:30) for a private guided sunrise hike or camel ride to the top of the highest dune in Erg Chebbi — watch the Sahara come alive in the first light of day, a truly transcendent experience. Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast in the dunes. After breakfast, explore the Merzouga village and the Dayet Srji salt lake — a seasonal flamingo habitat. Visit a local Gnawa musician's home for a private cultural music session and tea ceremony.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional premium desert activities: private sandboarding on the dunes, a 4x4 dune-bashing excursion with an expert local driver, or a guided walk to a nomadic Berber family encampment for an authentic cultural exchange. Visit the Khamlia village — home to the Gnawa people, descendants of sub-Saharan African slaves — for a private Gnawa music performance. Begin the return journey toward Marrakech, stopping in the Todra Gorge — a spectacular 300m-high limestone canyon — for a late afternoon walk along the canyon floor.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a luxury kasbah hotel in the Dades Valley or Boumalne Dades area (e.g., Kasbah Panorama or Xaluca Dades) for the night. Enjoy a candlelit dinner on the kasbah terrace with views of the illuminated canyon walls.

meals.breakfast: Berber breakfast at the desert camp — msemen, amlou, fresh dates, Moroccan tea, eggs cooked over an open fire, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the camp — packed with Moroccan sandwiches, olives, cheese, fruit, and fresh juice; enjoyed in the shade of the dunes or at a roadside oasis
meals.dinner: Kasbah hotel restaurant dinner — traditional Moroccan menu: bissara (fava bean soup), chicken tagine with preserved lemon, Dades Valley lamb chops, and chebakia (honey-sesame pastry) with mint tea

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise dune experience is the highlight of the entire trip — do not miss it. Dress in warm layers for the pre-dawn excursion. The Todra Gorge is most dramatic in the late afternoon light. Confirm your kasbah accommodation in advance — options in the Dades Valley are limited and book quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the Dades Valley after breakfast and continue the scenic return drive to Marrakech via the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the Skoura Oasis — a vast palmery dotted with ancient kasbahs — for a guided walk through the palm groves and a visit to the 17th-century Kasbah Amerhidil (featured on the 50-dirham banknote). Continue through the Draa Valley, stopping at a traditional argan oil cooperative run by a Berber women's collective — participate in a demonstration of traditional argan oil extraction and purchase premium cold-pressed argan oil directly from the source.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by mid-afternoon. Check back in to Hotel Aday and freshen up. Spend the afternoon exploring the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) in depth — visit the historic Jewish cemetery, the Lazama Synagogue, and the covered market. Browse the high-end concept stores and artisan boutiques along Rue de la Liberté and in the Gueliz neighborhood (Marrakech's modern French quarter) for premium Moroccan crafts, leather goods, and designer kaftans.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the legendary La Mamounia Hotel bar — one of the world's great hotel bars, frequented by Winston Churchill and countless celebrities. Dinner at Le Tobsil — a legendary Marrakchi restaurant set in a 17th-century riad, offering a fixed-price traditional Moroccan feast considered one of the finest dining experiences in the country. Live Andalusian music accompanies the meal.

meals.breakfast: Full kasbah breakfast before departure — fresh-baked bread, local honey, Berber omelette with herbs, seasonal fruit, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch at a traditional Berber restaurant in the Draa Valley — mechoui lamb, Moroccan salads, and fresh-baked bread; simple but authentic
meals.dinner: Le Tobsil, 22 Derb Moulay Abdallah Ben Hezzian — fixed-price Moroccan feast (approximately 700–900 MAD per person); includes multiple courses of cold salads, pastilla, tagine, couscous, and dessert; reservations essential and must be made weeks in advance

day_by_day.notes: Le Tobsil is one of Marrakech's most sought-after dinner reservations — book as early as possible, ideally before your trip begins. La Mamounia bar has a smart-casual dress code. The argan oil cooperative visit is a meaningful cultural experience and supports local Berber women's economic empowerment — purchase directly to ensure fair trade.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the riad. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (non-Muslims cannot enter the mosque but the gardens and exterior are stunning) for a peaceful morning stroll. Explore the Cyber Parc Arsat Moulay Abdeslam — a beautiful public garden adjacent to the Medina walls, perfect for a quiet morning walk. Last-minute luxury shopping at the Ensemble Artisanal — a government-run fixed-price artisan market where you can purchase authentic Moroccan crafts (zellige tiles, leather goods, silver jewelry, Berber rugs) at fair prices without bargaining pressure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final hammam session at a premium spa — book the Royal Hammam experience at Les Bains de Marrakech or the Hammam de la Rose for a 2-hour luxury treatment: traditional kessa scrub, ghassoul mask, argan oil massage, and rose water rinse. Return to the hotel for final packing and checkout. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Enjoy a final mint tea at the airport lounge before boarding. Carry home memories of the Sahara sunrise, the labyrinthine souks, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final riad breakfast — the full spread: fresh orange juice, mint tea, msemen, baghrir, amlou, honey, fresh fruit, Moroccan pastries, and soft-boiled eggs
meals.lunch: Al Fassia Restaurant, Gueliz — one of Marrakech's finest traditional restaurants, run entirely by women; try the pigeon pastilla, lamb with caramelized onions and prunes, and the milk bastilla dessert; approximately 500–800 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight — or if time permits, a final glass of Moroccan rosé wine and a mezze platter at a Gueliz wine bar before the transfer

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in — Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy. Confirm your checkout time with Hotel Aday and arrange luggage storage if your flight is late. Declare any argan oil, spices, or food items at customs if returning to the US. The Ensemble Artisanal is an excellent last-stop for authentic, fairly priced souvenirs without the souk bargaining stress.
